declaration: Law-1 visible parked channel. ZERO of the 9 input candidates (DEV26-01..09) were quality-filtered, dropped, or withheld by this stage. All 9 are accounted for in deduped-findings.json: 5 unique, 4 collapsed onto existing ledger fingerprints with full justification and traceable `duplicateOf` targets. Nothing went to /dev/null. The single entry parked below did not come from the candidate list — it is an item the script-auditor placed in `refutedOrNotFiled` whose refutation is, on review, incomplete, and which therefore should not rest solely in a not-filed list.

parked.originalId: refutedOrNotFiled[0] — 'The second clean:local deletes the RUNNING anvil's tmp state (closure hazard EH-01)'
parked.source: script-auditor refuted list, re-routed by the deduplicator
parked.reason: PARTIALLY-REFUTED, NOT FULLY REFUTED. The observed-consequence half is solidly negative and is not disputed: ~/.foundry/anvil/tmp/ was sampled every 0.5s for 30s spanning BOTH clean:local runs and was empty at all 60 samples; anvil in this invocation (no --state, no --fork-url) never writes there; the chain survived, all 381 broadcast transactions landed, and it was still mining at block 799. But the script-auditor itself records an UNTESTED branch in the same breath: whether a concurrently-running FORKED anvil belonging to another task would have state in that directory was never exercised. A `rm -rf` inside a project script that reaches OUTSIDE the repository into shared per-user state, with an untested destructive branch, is not something that should live only in a refuted list under Law 1 — recall beats tidiness. It is parked here rather than filed as a finding because no consequence was observed and none is claimed, and filing it as a finding on an untested branch would overstate it.
parked.proposedSeverity: qa / informational — code smell with an untested destructive branch
parked.whyNotFiled: No demonstrated impact. The forked-anvil branch is a hypothesis, and the project bars speculation on undemonstrated root cause. Filing would be overstatement; deleting would be a Law-1 recall failure. Parking is the correct third option.
parked.toResolve: Cheap and decisive: start a second `anvil --fork-url $RPC_MAINNET --state <dir>` alongside, run `clean:local`, and observe whether the forked instance's state files are removed. One command settles it either way.
parked.recommendationIfConfirmed: Scope the cleanup to the repository: drop `rm -rf ~/.foundry/anvil/tmp/*` from `clean:local` entirely, or replace it with a targeted removal of this project's own anvil state path. A project script should never rm -rf a shared user directory it does not own.
